corrections.form_value: participants.n_analyzed = 50; Experimental class n_analyzed = 25; Control class n_analyzed = 25; criterion_2_at_least_50_people = met
corrections.source_says: The document states a research sample of 50 students, with 25 in each group, but does not separately state how many completed the posttest or entered the reported analyses. Retain 50 and 25 per group as reported sample counts in the description; under the instruction not to infer counts, the analyzed counts should be null and criterion 2 unclear. There is no reported attrition count, so neither a loss below 50 nor complete retention can be confirmed. The randomized counts correctly remain null, and core eligibility remains no because assignment was nonrandom.
corrections.quote: The total number of research subjects was 50 fifth-grade students, divided into two groups:
corrections.locator: p. 809 (PDF p. 6), Research participants; pp. 812-815 (PDF pp. 9-12), Tables 3 and 5-8 provide no analyzed sample counts

corrections.source_says: The three experts validated the research instruments before use; the paper does not identify the people or system that scored the students' stories. Instrument validation does not establish expert rating of the outcomes. Set measure to null and explain in measure_detail that a writing rubric was used but scorer identity and expertise are not stated. The form's eligibility.reason already acknowledges this uncertainty.

corrections.form_value: question = with_ai for S1-O1, S1-O2 and S1-O3; ai_available_when_produced empty; open_questions = []
corrections.source_says: The procedures distinguish ChatGPT-supported lessons from the subsequent posttest but do not state whether AI was available while the scored posttest stories were written. The phrase assessed using ChatGPT engineering prompts on p. 813 is ambiguous and does not resolve access during production. The with_ai versus after_ai classification is therefore unconfirmed: use null for question and ai_available_when_produced and record the uncertainty in open_questions. Do not infer either AI removal or continued access.
corrections.quote: administering a posttest to both the experimental and control classes to determine the improvement in ethnoliteracy-based fictional story writing skills in fifth-grade elementary school students.
corrections.locator: p. 809 (PDF p. 6), Research Procedures, implementation stage (b)-(c); p. 813 (PDF p. 10), paragraph preceding Table 5

corrections.form_value: {"paper_design_summary": "Fifty fifth-grade students at one public elementary school in Cimahi, Indonesia, were in two nonequivalent classes of 25: one class took ethnoliteracy-based fiction-writing lessons with structured ChatGPT prompting, and the other took conventional lessons without AI. Both classes wrote a fiction story as a pretest and a posttest, scored on an eight-indicator rubric (structure, plot cohesion, setting, characters, message, creativity of language style, local cultural values, spelling). The paper reports indicator means per class, N-gain, and one independent-samples t-test on the posttest.", "S1-O1.name": "Posttest fiction-writing skill score (overall, eight-indicator rubric)", "one_line_finding": "Posttest fiction-writing scores did not differ significantly between the ChatGPT class and the conventional class (t = -0.538, df = 50, two-tailed sig = 0.593; p. 815, Table 8), although indicator means favored the ChatGPT class (local cultural values 60 vs 38, creativity of language style 52 vs 49; Table 5, pp. 813-814) and N-gain was 0.069 vs 0.062 (p. 814)."}
corrections.source_says: All copied numerical values match the PDF, but Table 8 does not identify its outcome as an overall eight-indicator posttest score or identify the test as an independent-samples posttest comparison. Its variable is labelled Reading Comprehension, the methods mention both paired and independent tests, and the text below the table calls it one-tailed although the table says sig (2-tailed). Qualify the outcome name and design summary, and make the one-line finding attribute the printed nonsignificant result to this ambiguously labelled table. Preserve t = -0.538, df = 50 and sig (2-tailed) = 0.593 as printed, together with the preceding prose's contradictory 0.0593 and significance claim; do not present the test's outcome/timepoint as established. The descriptive posttest means and N-gains in the finding require no numerical changes.
corrections.locator: p. 811 (PDF p. 8), Data Analysis Techniques; p. 815 (PDF p. 12), Table 8 and paragraphs immediately before and after it

corrections.form_value: Only S1-O1 overall fiction-writing score, S1-O2 creativity of language style and S1-O3 local cultural values are listed; notes empty
corrections.source_says: Other scored dimensions of narrative quality are omitted despite form-spec rule 7. Table 5 reports experimental/control posttest means for story structure 74/65, plot cohesion 80/64, setting 82/58, characters/characterization 63/54 and message 52/49; Table 3 gives their respective pretest means as 41/40, 40/36, 42/37, 39/33 and 31/36. These are distinct rubric outcomes, not robustness variants. Add the relevant narrative-quality outcomes, with scorer and AI availability left unresolved. Spelling is also reported (posttest 60/49; pretest 36/36); if excluded as a technical writing measure outside creativity, state that scope decision in notes. No SDs or indicator-specific tests are supplied.
corrections.quote: The story has a setting that describes time, place, and atmosphere.

corrections.source_says: The identified study comparison is Experimental class (ChatGPT-supported lessons) versus Control class (conventional lessons without AI), corresponding to ai_vs_bau under the codebook, while retaining the nonrandomized design. Fill these arm and comparison fields for the indicator comparisons. For S1-O2 and S1-O3, direction is treatment_higher for the descriptive posttest means only; significance of these indicators is not tested. S1-O1 can record the printed Table 8 result as no_clear_difference and statistics_available = [test_statistic], with the outcome/timepoint caveat above rather than an unqualified posttest contrast. Describe means-only availability for the indicators without implying that SDs or analyzed Ns were reported.

confirmed: The complete markdown was read through the references, and cited numerical passages were checked in the PDF. This is the 20-page journal article in International Journal of Language Education 9(4), 2025, pp. 804-823, published 30 December 2025; DOI 10.26858/ijole.v1i2.82102 (PDF p. 1).
The document title and five authors match source.title_on_document and source.authors_on_document (p. 804, PDF p. 1).

One nonequivalent-control-group study explicitly did not involve randomization; both groups received pretests and posttests. quasi_people, assignment.randomized = no, core = no and context_class = observational are supported (p. 808, PDF p. 5, Research design).

The reported research sample comprises 50 people, 25 in each group, rather than 50 texts or ratings; these are not randomized counts or separately documented analysis counts (p. 809, PDF p. 6, Research participants).

Participants were fifth-grade pupils, on average 10-11 years old, at Cimahi Mandiri 3 Public Elementary School in Cimahi City, West Java; sampling was purposive (p. 809, PDF p. 6, Research participants).

Students produced fiction-writing pretests and posttests assessed using eight writing indicators, including creativity of language style and local cultural values; criterion 3 is supported by scores on written output (pp. 809-813, PDF pp. 6-10, procedures, rubric and Tables 3 and 5).

S1-O2 reported values are exact: language-style creativity pretest means 38 experimental versus 35 control, and posttest means 52 versus 49, both posttest categories Very less (p. 812, PDF p. 9, Table 3 row 6; p. 813, PDF p. 10, Table 5 row 6).

S1-O3 reported values are exact: local-cultural-values pretest means 25 experimental versus 35 control; posttest 60 (Not enough) versus 38 (Very less) (p. 812, PDF p. 9, Table 3 row 7; p. 814, PDF p. 11, Table 5 row 7).
N-gain is printed as 0.069 for the experimental class and 0.062 for the control class, both low category; these are not standardized mean differences (p. 814, PDF p. 11, paragraph following Table 5).
Table 8 prints Reading Comprehension, Thitung = -0.538, Df = 50, sig (2-tailed) = 0.593 and H0 is accepted. All these values in S1-O1.reported match the PDF (p. 815, PDF p. 12, Table 8).

The paragraph before Table 8 prints 0.0593 and says Ha is accepted; the paragraph after it says there is no significant difference in fiction-writing skills. The form correctly preserves that contradiction (p. 815, PDF p. 12).
Every numerical value in the existing one_line_finding matches Tables 5 and 8 and the N-gain paragraph; the correction concerns the certainty of the test identification (pp. 813-815, PDF pp. 10-12).

Tables 3 and 5 report indicator means without SDs or indicator-specific inferential tests; no confidence intervals or standardized treatment effects are supplied for those indicators (pp. 812-815, PDF pp. 9-12).
This is an original nonrandomized classroom study, not a synthesis; the empty synthesis fields are appropriate (pp. 808-811, PDF pp. 5-8).

No appendix or supplementary material is identified in the document; the final pages are references, so supplement.exists = not_stated and in_this_pdf = false are supported (complete PDF, especially pp. 820-823, PDF pp. 17-20).

The paper declares no conflict of interest and acknowledges Indonesian ministry funding and educational institutions, with no company involvement reported (p. 820, PDF p. 17, Declaration of conflicting interest and Funding acknowledgements).
summary: The paper reports 50 pupils in a nonrandomized classroom comparison, so it remains observational context and contains no randomized people study. All copied result numbers match the PDF, but analyzed counts, scorer identity, AI availability and the identification of Table 8 are overstated or unresolved, and outcome and comparison fields are incomplete.
